spec.summary: Two players alternate placing X and O on a 3×3 grid; three in a row wins, and a full board without a win is a draw.

initial_setup.description: Every cell is empty; X moves first, with no winner or draw.

actions.legal_when: There is no winner or draw, x and y are each within 0 through 2, and board[y][x] is empty.
actions.effect: Set board[y][x] to the current player's value. Check for a win, then a draw; only if neither occurs, switch the current player from 1 to 2 or from 2 to 1. An illegal placement returns false without changing state.

actions.legal_when: An R keydown is received; the source imposes no game-state restriction.
actions.effect: Reset the board, current player, winner, and draw state to their initial values.

actions.legal_when: Escape is pressed or a window-close event is received.
actions.effect: Stop the application loop; no game outcome is assigned.

outcomes.condition: After a placement, any row, column, or either diagonal has all three cells equal to the current player's value.
After a placement, no winning line exists and every board cell is nonzero.

controls.control: Left-button down; convert pointer position to a cell using the board's left and top offsets and cell size.

presentation.description: A Pygame window displays a status line showing the turn, winner, or draw; instructions; and a 3×3 board of rounded cells with blue X marks and orange O marks. The display loop is capped at 60 frames per second.

assumptions: The action's target coordinate represents the source's x and y parameters. Winner and draw are derived from the board rather than stored as separate state variables.

value.name: Plane carrier for blue X mark

value.reason: The specified plane primitives are carriers only; the source does not define procedural mesh geometry that would make them visibly depict the X and O glyphs or the rounded cells.

assumptions: The supplied inventory contains source and documentation files but no presentation asset files, so no file assets are declared.
The unit-sized planes are normalized procedural carriers, not claims about the source window's dimensions or finished glyph geometry.

The supplied prefab and camera shapes are scene defaults, not a reconstruction of the Pygame drawing code. The cube geometry and symbolic cell variants do not reproduce its rounded cells or X and O marks.

assumptions: The primary mouse press supplies the selected board cell as event_data.rule_coordinate after converting the pointer position using the board offsets and cell size. Window-close events are handled by the host and need no binding.

issues.problem: Escape is bound to quit, but the source also quits when the window-close event occurs; input_ir has no window-close binding.
issues.fix: Bind the window-close event to the existing quit host_command intent.
